utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, you're to continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you and to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember yesterday when we left, we were talking about an incident where you were under sniper fire on the 15th of April, 1995. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I want to ask you a couple of more questions about that incident. Firstly, you were saying that you had been in touch with the headquarters at the PTT during that one and a half hours; do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you give the -- did you give your position to headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did give my position that I was under fire in front of Holiday Inn, and this was also being listened to by a liaison officer and a liaison officer on Lima side, and he was also listening since we were operating on the same channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say Lima side, do you mean the Bosnian Serb side?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, while you were coming under sniper fire, were there any soldiers of the Bosnian government in your vicinity?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nobody. Earlier there were two APCs from the French battalion of the anti-sniping team which were supposed to be deployed there; and once we came under fire, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were there any Bosnian government tanks or other military facilities in the vicinity of the place where you were being sniped at?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing of that sort. I couldn't see any Bosnian soldier in the vicinity. The road was almost empty since it was a dangerous road. Only we had two French APCs, as I already mentioned. I heard here during this sniping activity, which we were experiencing, one of the patrol of our UNMO team passed through. It was coming from the PTT side and going towards the old part of the city. They also got a couple of impacts; but since the car had armoured protection, nothing happened to them. But they also confirmed that they did experience an impact and same was reported, too, by them to our duty officer in the PTT building. And since they were using the same channel, I also heard and I also communicated the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just stick to the incident where you were under sniper fire. I want to ask you, at that time, apart from the sniper fire coming from, as you said, the Metalka building, was there any other military activity going on in that area?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Given your answers to these previous questions, are you able to make an assessment as to whether you were the target of the sniper fire from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, I was a target. Not only me; along with me, the entire patrol from my team, which at that time comprised of another UNMO and an interpreter and myself, because we could see and hear impact on the anti-sniping screen behind which we had taken cover. It was being hit and also a couple of bullets went over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In the one and a half hours that you were under sniper fire, did the anti-sniping screen hinder or obstruct your view of the origin of the sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, once we got behind it, we couldn't see the sniper. However, initially I saw the fire -- the fire was coming from that Metalka building; and in between when there was some lull between the two shots, though there were more than two shots, I could peep from left or right of this anti-sniping screen, and during that I could some movement in Metalka building. But I do confirm that first time once I was on the fork-lift carrying out investigation, once I reached there, I was fired upon from Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that you were with another UNMO team member and an interpreter. What gender was the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interpreter was Mr. Faruk, a male, and also a Jordanian UNMO, Major Alsweety [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was the interpreter wearing military or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes; but also along with that, flakjacket provided by UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the uniform you were wearing, was it a standard United Nations uniforms.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military observers were not supposed to wear United Nations standard military uniform. I was wearing my country's uniform. It was total camouflage, shirt and trouser. I was wearing blue beret and blue helmet. The beret was underneath the helmet. Also, I had insignia on my arm that was from the United Nations. Moreover, we reached there in the blue -- blue flag, white, soft-skin United Nations vehicle was UN, and United Nations Military Observer was clearly marked and blue flag was very much visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, when I asked you where the fire had come from, you said the Metalka building. And I asked you how did you know that, and you said: "Because I could see somebody moving in those windows of this building and then firing." I want to tell the Court what did you see?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw one I was on the fork-lift I had just reached. I went to the fork-lift, and I had to step about three or four steps up and then into the cabin which had holes in the rear. When I said the rear, the glass behind the driver head and the front screen. So I was getting into that, and naturally it was facing towards Metalka building. When I say the fork-lift, the fork was facing towards Metalka building, and also I assume that the driver while sitting in the fork-lift was also facing Metalka building and same was my position, too. I never sat on that driver seat, but I was half in, half out of that cabin, and I was looking from that side when I was fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I want you to concentrate on what you say in the building. You said you saw someone moving around. Were you able to make out what that person was wearing?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible to see him what he was wearing because it was early part of the day; I mean before midday. And inside it was dark and outside it was almost sunshine, so it was not possible. But I could see someone moving and earlier he had fired upon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, after this incident on the 15th of April, did you undertake an investigation of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The very next day and also it happened on 15th of April. 16th and 17th of April, I was instructed by my headquarters to visit the sites with the French soldiers from the French battalion, which I did, and I visited the site. When I said the site, it was the same lane and the location where the fork-lift was, and we went towards -- to the river, came back, saw. Also we went in one of the building because French wanted to see, and this was my assessment, they wanted the to see whether the fire came from that building or not. That building was under the control of Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. This is --

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. Let's take this investigation, you talk about on the 16th and 17th, slowly and careful. On the 16th of April, you were tasked by area headquarters to do an investigation, and who did you do that investigation with?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the French soldiers from the French bat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why did you accompany the French soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the instructions from my UNMO headquarters that have I to accompany them. I was not supposed -- I was not asked to write a separate investigation report, but I was to facilitate them and accompany them, and that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on the 16th of April, you went to buildings that were on the Bosnian government side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the building under Bosnian side, in the same lane, towards the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why did you go to a building on the Bosnian government side?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because French asked me to take us to the building and with our coordination it was possible to go inside the building and see. We went upstairs and few windows, they checked. They stood and looked towards where the incident took place. That is where the fork-lift was hit where a French soldier had died.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went into the building on the Bosnian government side, did you see any evidence of military activity, any sniper weapons or weapons like that, when you went there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to have the witness look at 65 ter 2825, the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph as the one that you marked on yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you, first of all, point to the building on the Bosnian government side that you went to visit on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet, I can point out. This is the building where we went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you take a pen and just put a cross or a circle round it, please.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is putting a circle around the building on the Bosnian government side that he went to visit on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on the 17th of April, did you visit any buildings on the Bosnian Serb side in respect to this incident?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On 17th of April, that was the next day to this investigation, we visited red building; and when I say red building, red building on both the sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you only visit the red building or did you visit another building?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you put a cross by the red building that you visited on the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, sir, first, I have to point out simply I have to mark that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: First, if you know where it is, please mark it.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This is the red building. I want to make a mention here, this was the building where less than half occupied by the BiH and more than half occupied by the Serbs and divided by a portion of it which was building -- now, if I look at it from left of the centre of this building, collapsed. So both sides were occupying this very building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around the Metalka building as well.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went to the Metalka building, did you see any evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, if he puts a circle around both buildings, how will we differentiate them later on, maybe a letter M or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put a letter M by the Metalka building, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in addition, I would like him to show in which place Muslim forces were in which part of that building, and in which part of the building there were forces of army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because he said there were both representatives of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and representatives of the VRS. Could you please show where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you have a time to question the witness. It's for the Prosecutor to lead the evidence in the way that he considers best suited for his case. If you wish to have him do that, then let him do; and perhaps he might as well just do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I am happy to ask him to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can you do that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have drawn circles around Metalka building and marked M under that circle. And, Your Honour, sir, do you want me to also draw a circle around the red building and writing letter R on top of it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, sir. And, Your Honour, sir, do you want me to draw which portion of the building was under the control of BiH and which was the portion of the building under Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So if I'll permitted, sir, may I draw letter B where BiH was having control on part of the building and S on the part of the building which was under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be appropriate. But may I ask you, Mr. Butt, earlier you told us that you were not allowed to go to the -- to the BiH because you're a Muslim. But if I understand you, you -- your evidence now is that you went there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If I am permitted, I draw and then I read how I went. Sir, after the incident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, but I'm -- I'm not having any French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Nor me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you try again, please, Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it any better now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have just explained to us that there is a red building with on one side, ABiH units and on the other side VRS units. At this stage, could you show us that confrontation line? Trace it for to us to distinguish, because I find it hard now to distinguish where both armies are. Could you trace this confrontation line on this picture. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sir, definitely it is very much possible. May I submit to the Honourable Court, if this picture can be a little bit enlarged, so I with easily draw the confrontation line. If it is possible, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that possible? The court deputy I'm asking. He is shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand if it is moved, the picture will be wiped clean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, I regret to say that it can't be done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, sir, then I request that I should be allowed to draw the confrontation line with different colour, if that is possible, because it might be clear some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, different colour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The building as I have already -- the red building, with the-- encircled and on top of that I have written letter R. If I look at it, on the left side I have also written letter Bravo, B. This portion up till where the building is collapsed, almost halfway, was under BiH control; and on the right, after the portion or beyond the portion which had collapsed, portion of this building was with -- under Serb control. And this blue line, confrontation line was passing through this collapsed portion of the building and going over this building and then turning right, along the southern side of the river, up to -- there's a building, I don't remember the name. It is north of Grbavica stadium almost straight. If that portion is shown, I may also be able to draw the confrontation line. However, this was the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps you should mark the confrontation line maybe CL.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm doing that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please follow up on the President's question as to how was it possible to access this Serb-held territory despite the fact that you, as you told us yesterday, would normally be barred from entering that territory.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true, sir. That happened on the 27th of February, but this was after this soldier was killed. Through Lima and through my headquarters, it was possible for me to go across the confrontation line for only the investigation. And I accompanied and I was taken to the Metalka building and to the portion of the red building under control Serbs, by the local Serb probably company commander or the platoon commander, whomsoever it was. We crossed the confrontation line. We came from the Grbavica side. And later on, on the left, which is under BiH control, we went in that part of the building also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you clarify one more thing for the Chamber; namely, how did the confrontation line look like behind the building that was just left of the Metalka building. Were there some sort of fence set up in the streets or is it -- was the confrontation line just something that everybody knew was there but it wasn't visible otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. There was nothing of that sort like fence or any line drawn physically on the ground. It was understood area under BiH control and area front of that under Serb control; between that a kind of imaginary line would pass and that would be considered as confrontation line. And the closest area where the -- both the warring factions were eyeball to eyeball that was red building, where they were only apart the by about 30 or 40 feet; whereas, at places they were about 100 feet, 100 yards, and some places 70, 80 feet apart. It depended on the occupation of both the -- of various buildings by both of the warring factions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know how the population lived in the area would know about the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very much clear to them that people living on the BiH side and people living on the Serb side what are the areas with the respective warring faction, and accordingly they would move and approach different areas, a market, or wherever they wanted to go. So they were well clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would the confrontation line have been manned in that area that we're dealing in its entirety by -- by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. This was not like that. On the left of where this confrontation line is coming vertical, on the left of that, is a place, Vrbanja bridge. There was a French post and observation post. Also it had a couple of APCs permanently deployed there. They would take care of that area. Also, the anti-sniping team deployed all along these vertical lanes coming towards north from the Miljacka river; and then further on towards the right that is west of this area on Grbavica stadium and bridge, there were also various posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, it's striking me that the term "confrontation line" can you quite misleading. It would suggest to one that you have a line that is manned by soldiers with -- with weapons, but in fact it -- it is an imaginary line, and it may not in some parts be manned by soldiers. In other part it is may have soldiers. So the real inquiry for us in terms of the evidence shouldn't be focussed on whether fire came from the confrontation lines, but whether fire came from a place where the soldiers were and who were those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have just two remarks on your observation. Firstly, the Prosecution is calling Bosnian government, former Bosnian government military personnel to -- to give accurate -- or to give evidence as to the location of confrontation lines. And, secondly, the Prosecution, in its indictment, alleges that the fire came from territory that there is no dispute that it was in Bosnian Serb territory; in other words, either well beyond the confrontation lines or -- or in an area where it is -- without dispute controlled by the Bosnian Serbs. And this is the evidence that we are going to be submitting to go Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Butt.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I could probably convey it that troops or soldiers I was making mention of, those were of United Nations. On this imaginary line on both sides, on the side of the Serb they had their troops occupying all these buildings. And on the BiH side, they also had their positions. So all along the confrontation line, very thickly and heavy deployment of warring factions had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So this area of the confrontation line was manned --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by both the warring factions. I was referring to the UNPROFOR troops. I stand corrected, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we can have this photograph admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P223, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, in an answer to Their Honours, you mentioned the Vrbanja bridge and spoke about two APCs being there. When you spoke about the APCs, did you mean APCs of the French forces of the United Nations or did you mean APCs of the Bosnian government?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these were of the French battalion. They had their permanent post here and couple of APCs deployed and also had an observation post right next to the Vrbanja bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I wanted to talk to you about your visit to the Metalka building. First, you told the Court that you went there with an official of the Bosnian Serb army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did the fact that a French soldier was killed and that you accompanied a French soldier enable you to get access to the Serb side on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very right. It was through Lima, the military observer liaison officer on the Lima side and the efforts from our headquarters that this visit took place, and I accompanied the French soldiers carrying out this investigation and I went on the other side of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that you were under sniper fire for an hour and a half and that the fire came from Metalka building. When you went to the Metalka building on the 17th of April, what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Metalka building, there were few soldiers having their weapons as it was a routine, and firing positions like any other building would have on both the sides in this area that all -- that I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right. I'm not asking you about any other building. I just want you to stick to what you saw at the Metalka building. You said you saw a few soldiers. First, let's be clear. Were those soldiers Bosnian Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were Serb soldiers carrying their rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Given your military experience, did the position appear to you to be one that was -- that had been there for some time or was it a position that was quickly established? Did it have any characteristics of long-term use?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to be under the use of those troops for quite some time, because towards the rear of the building, away from the -- where the confrontation line was, they had made a few places where they could make coffee or tea or things like that, and they had quite a few sandbags near the windows, facing the other side of the confrontation line and those firing positions from where -- in their eventuality they would fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said they had quite a few sandbags near the windows facing the other side of the confrontation line. Did the windows enable a clear view of the position you were at when you were under sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. From quite a few windows, it was quite possible to engage that fork-lift where later on I was lying behind the sniping screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just because we in the Court are not experts in military terminology, when you say "engage the fork-lift," do you mean, to put it in layman's terms, to shoot at the fork-lift?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, sir. It was possible from that building from a couple -- more than a couple of windows from the upper floors to engage fork-lift, that I could visualize because the fork-lift that they had had already been removed. But I could see the anti-sniping screens there, which could be engaged, so that was clearly understood that that fork-lift could have been also engaged, if anybody want to the fire from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You also said that you visited the Bosnian Serb side of the red building. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you also see evidence of a military position when you went there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. Like Serbs, Bosnian also had a soldiers firing positions, soldiers carrying -- soldiers carrying --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I cannot follow English, it was interpreted to me as "Serbs." Did the witness, in fact, want to refer to the members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? It was interpreted to me as "Serbs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just repeat the question you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, please just listen very carefully to the question. You said that on that day you went to the Metalka building. You also said that you went to the Bosnian Serb side of the red building; do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you went to the Bosnian Serb side of the red building, did you see evidence of -- of a military position there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir. And a portion of the red building under ABiH control was also occupied by the soldiers. They also had their firing positions, like fixing sandbags, and soldiers were also carrying their rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think we need -- I need to ask you that question again, and I need you, Mr. Witness, to again listen very carefully. You have already given evidence that you went to the Metalka building on the Bosnian Serb territory where you saw evidence of sniping positions. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you see on the photograph on your screen where you have indicated the red building under Bosnian Serb territory. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir, with letter B.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about the building -- the part of the building under Bosnian Serb territory where you have actually written RS?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: S only. R is for the red building. S is for the Serb portion of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. So I want you to concentrate on your visit to the Serb portion of the building. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you went to that portion of the building, did you see evidence of sniping positions there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not sniping position as I understand as a military man. That sniping positions are the normal firing positions, but little comfortable from there, sniper taking his time can engage his target, and I saw the firing position in this Metalka building which could engage the position of the fork-lift.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why do you say "not a anti-sniping position as you understand as a military man."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sniping position, there is no difference between sniping position where sniper can take his time under cover and can engage the target that is a sniping position, it could be any firing position. And that is what I have said, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But I guess the continuation of this question is whether you actually saw snipers with sniping weapons. I understand that a sniper's weapon would be a rifle with a -- with a telescope. So the question is: Did you see any sniping equipment or sniping armory in the red building and also in the Metalka building when you were there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. In none of the buildings, I could see, during my visit to these buildings, any rifle fitted with telescope to become a sniper rifle. It was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, from the Metalka building to where you were on the 15th of April, what is roughly the distance?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, distance where I was lying behind the sniping -- anti-sniping screen and the firing position in the Metalka building, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be 250, 275 metres, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your experience as a military person, is it possible with -- is it possible to engage a target from that distance without an optical telescope?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is very much possible to engage the target on this -- at this range from ordinary rifle and, of course, with the rifle mounted on telescope -- telescope on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just let me get that clear now. Your evidence is all that you saw in the Metalka building was weaponry that could engage the fork-lift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is very true. And it was day after that incident had taken happened, very next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I just want to take Mr. President -- Mr. President's question a bit further. Is it also possible from that distance to engage a human being, as opposed to fork-lift, from that distance with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is very much possible that a human being at about 275 yards can be engaged with ordinary rifle also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that you went to buildings on the Bosnian government side to establish whether the firing had come from the Bosnian government side. What did you establish?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was not to conduct any kind of investigation, I was only ordered to accompany the French. But from their assessment, I could make out that they were more focussed on the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your time with the United Nations in Sarajevo, did you ever investigate or come across reports that concluded that the Bosnian government was firing on their own people?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two clear incidents which I took it that probably a few people do think that BiH government is targeting its own people. One was this very incident -- this French incident that we went across French soldiers killing incident. We went across and also we went to the BiH under control buildings. Second was somewhere in July, Mr. Mike O'Connor, a journalist by profession representing New York times, U.S. based, and International Herald Tribune, Paris based, interviewed me with the specific permission from my senior military observer, Colonel Pilan [phoen] from the headquarters. On that day, I received a telephone call from my senior military observer that a journalist was to visit my team location, he should be briefed about the situation and, whatsoever, question he has, it is my decision to answer that. My reply to Colonel Pilan was that, Sir, was I supposed to give interviews to the press people; and he -- his reply was that, Yes, I'm permitted and I can give the interview. On 13th of July, he came at about 10.00 until about 2.00, 2.30, had his lunch, we sat together, and then we discussed. I then realized he was -- Mr. Mike O'Conner was of the view that BiH government is sniping its own people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What was your reply to him?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a lengthy discussion. I asked him because I was really surprised it was a news, though this French incident I had at the back of my mind. I asked him, "Could you tell me the buildings on the BiH side from where the BiH soldiers under the instructions of BiH government are sniping its own people?" In reply, he gave me four buildings, which included parliament building also, the tall building on the left side of this picture which is being shown to me at this very moment. I asked him that all of buildings you have taken the name, have you seen those buildings from inside, that it is possible to snipe from those buildings. He said, no; and then my reply was that I had by that time spent about eight, nine months in very area, was well familiar with the area, that "most of the buildings you are referring to do not have clear-cut field of fire to engage on the own side." However, the building that is a parliament building, yes, it is possible. And I had incidentally before that visited that site, and I didn't find anything of that there, though soldiers were very much there on the top, couple of soldiers, and in the basement which was a little bit with the garbage and water. After that, about four, five hours interview, he left. And after about ten, fifteen days, I saw the report from the same gentleman appearing in one of the paper in Zagreb. I was on my CTO. And it was carrying a full scale page report that BiH government is sniping its own people. I went through that entire report and, to my utter surprise, there was no mention of time he had spent with me or he interviewed me and that was the end of it. However, after some time once I was back in Sarajevo, I saw the gentleman in the PTT building in the corridor. I asked him. He said that this was his view, his assessment, so he didn't feel obliged to talk about what transpired between myself and Mr. O'Conner. So he didn't include and than was end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you said that you went to the -- the parliament building and you said, "I had before that visited that site and I didn't find anything of that there." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers in the basement about four or five when I visited it; and then on the top floor, there were two soldiers sitting on the chairs. Of course, they were carrying their rifles. So this is all what I saw and, of course, we could observe this very building from our observation post. None of our observers had any kind of report that it was being used by any firer or sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is what I want you to stick to, if possible. Reports or your own investigations, did you ever come to a conclusion that the Bosnian government forces were sniping on their own people?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during my tenure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want to move from sniping and talk about shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Before we leave the sniping incidents, could we just ask the witness to clarify a bit about the French incident. I think the witness said that the French incident was an incident where a French UN soldier was killed, presumably by a Bosnian Muslim sniper; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a -- am I permitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This the impression that I gathered first. Once I had visited that building, which I have shown in the red circle in the lane, on this side of -- on the BiH side of the river, they were going into the windows and looking in the site where the soldier was hit. So I think anybody could understand probably they had some doubt in their mind that it came from this side. However, later on during the visit of Metalka, things were a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So why did you refer to the French incident as an incident in which Bosnian Muslim troops were supposed to snipe on their own people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, this was the reason, because the location where that French soldier was killed was being sniped. It was the hottest place and quite a few sniping incident had taken place. If there was a position in -- in any of the buildings, which was under BiH control, I think it could have been -- at least doubt could have been raised that probably they were also doing something. But it was not there on the ground. So it was not possible from that very building to engage that position where the fork-lift was standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not sure I understand your answer. My question was: Why did you refer to the French incident as an incident in which a UN soldier had been sniped by a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because with the French soldiers once we went for -- I went to complete them for the investigation, they visited buildings which were under BiH control; and then they were looking in those windows and then stand in those windows and looking towards that fork-lift where that soldier was hit. So it was quite clear that they had some doubts in their mind, probably fire came from this building or at least from this direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And it's conclusion was then, indeed, that the French soldier was not sniped by --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my assessment. But all I could see and observe, it was not possible. Also from the building which was under BiH control in the red circle, it was not possible from that building, as view was not clear of the fork-lift. So it was not possible from there. Once we visited there, it was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I think I know where there might be a misunderstanding or some confusion. In one of the answers to one of my questions about whether Bosnian government forces were firing upon themselves, the witness spoke about two incidents where people could think that fire came from the Bosnian government side; in other words, in my submission, there were two incidents of -- of speculation, as opposed to incidents that actually took place. I can point, Your Honours, to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, just before again we leave sniping, I just want to confirm one thing. When you were under sniper fire for one and a half hours, do you stand by your evidence that you saw fire coming from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see somebody firing from Metalka building towards where I was near that fork-lift. I do confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to shelling. In your period with the United Nations, can you say roughly how many incidents of shelling did you investigate?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be difficult, Your Honours, to give the exact figures. But these were quite in numbers. Our team used to carry out four to six impact investigation in a day; other day then maybe we have one. But at an average, four to six incidents per day were being investigated by my team. But there were a few days when we had a lot of impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And out of these incidents that you investigated, are you able to say how many involved civilian casualties?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These -- most of these investigations were -- which were impacts were on the residential or civil areas. On confrontation line, there were so many incidents, but we were not allowed. We were not supposed to carry out investigation in that area where the soldiers were engaging each other. So we didn't investigate. These are the incident that I'm referring to the area which were in the civil area, residential area, or the commercial area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And so in those residential or civil areas, the UNMO teams did not find military targets there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not; generally, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you know what a modified air bomb is?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could you very briefly explain to the Court what you know about modified air bomb?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Modified air bomb, the first time in my military life, I came across one was in my mission with United Nations in Sarajevo. This was a kind of bomb which was primarily air bomb made to be dropped from the aircraft. However, delivery means in Sarajevo was different. It was not the aircraft. In fact, about six to eight motors [Realtime transcript read in error "mortars"], motors were attached around its main body; and those were ignited putting it on some ram or platform, a slanting platform; and then giving the direction, the general direction you wanted to fire it, and it was free to go towards that direction. After it has been fired, nobody had any kind of control, any guidance to focus it or to keep it on the track towards its target.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I just ask you a clarification question. You said, in the transcript, "six to eight mortars, as in a m-o-r-t-a-r-s. Do you mean mortars or motors?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are the motors, m-o-t-o-r-s. Motors and not the mortars. Motors were attached, a kind of rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Bearing in mind your answer where you said, "Nobody had any kind of control any guidance to focus it or keep it on the track towards its target," and given your military experience, what could you say about the appropriateness of using these kind of weapons in an urban environment like Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that once you don't have any control on any projectile and even you can't direct it properly towards its target, the profit can only be to send it across towards the populated area where it goes hundred yards, 200 yards, doesn't matter, at least it can take on a building. And that kind of profit, you can grab it. Under pure military environment, it could hardly give you any good results.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say the profit could only be to send it across towards the populated area, are you saying that civilian casualties will be incurred?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. It had explosives in the -- in the shape of 100 kgs. It lands in any residential area. The urban area, as I have been asked, would definitely cause casualties in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recall any specific incidents of these modified air bombs that you investigated.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two incidents think I investigated. One was -- this very weapon was -- had an impact near our UNMO team accommodation in Hrasnica where a couple of UNMOs were injured; and about within a radius of 100 yards, buildings were severely damaged. One of our UNMO vehicle was blown up; of course, it was not occupied. Our armoured jeep also had a lot of damage, generator was blown off, and casualties to the civilians living around that accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When was that incident?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was I think in the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What was your role in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though this was not my area of responsibility, this incident took place at about 21.40 or 21.45 hours at night. Next day, my headquarters asked me to go and investigate, and I did investigate, as a couple of the UNMOs were injured and so they were not in good position to do the investigation. This was probably the reason I went there and I did the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did you determine in your investigation the direction of fire of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible to determine the exact and specific direction like we could determine in case of mortars and we could give the specific bearing, as it was without any kind of crater. But general direction could be given, keeping in mind that the impact or devastation it had caused to the building where it had landed and that it could only be possible to give the general direction, but not the specific bearing. It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your time with the United Nations in Sarajevo, did you ever see the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, the Bosnian government army, use these kinds of modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And the direction that you mentioned just in your previous sentence, that direction would be from which held territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General direct examination was from Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: From Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ilidza. It was the general direction. Specific bearing, sir, it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: We've just spoken about the incident in Hrasnica. Did you -- well, first I want to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, could I show the witness 65 ter 2341, and I'm interested, Mr. Registrar, pages 49 to 58.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a document on your screen there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm, sir. It is a special report from Sierra India 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where does this document come from.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is some report which has been sent by the team, that is Sierra India 1, and sent to Sierra X-ray, which is the headquarters duty officer. UNMO headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. Just to be clear, it's a document of the United Nations Military Observer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Butt. Did you hear that question, Mr. Butt? Is this a document of the United Nations Military Observer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I could be shown, Your Honour, sir, all the pages at least who has signed it, then I can confirm. But this, I can confirm that this is report from probably Sierra India 1. This is one of the UNMOs team in my time, and Sierra X-ray which was located at UNMO headquarters. This was address Valda, UNMO headquarter. But if I could be shown who has signed it, maybe I can further confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page. And if he can could leave it at that size.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, do you see four names and signatures on the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it would be only appropriate if I could see it in B/C/S. If I could see it too. Is displayed only in English. My colleague speaks English well, but I have no English at all. I only have some French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a translation for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, unfortunately at this moment it is currently being translated. It was sent yesterday for urgent translation and I apologise to learned counsel, but -- but perhaps I'll -- not actually going to ask the witness to go into details. I'm simply asking him to confirm that it is an UN document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was it on your list of documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it was

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, we have problems like these. Now and then you yourself will have a document not translated. It's a very short document, so we'll have the interpreters translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, but yesterday it wasn't in e-court. And it takes 48 hours for a document to enter e-court although it's on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, do you see -- do you see a page there with four names and signatures on them?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do see. And a couple of the UNMOs I do remember very vividly. They were very much there. And I think it is signed by them, so it does become a valid UN document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we can just go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I don't understand why we should go back to page 1 if he confirmed only the identity of the person who signed it and the authenticity of the document. I do not contest the authenticity, but the witness has nothing more to say about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the question you want to find out? What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, the question, Mr. President, is I want the witness to read the subject of the document so it can be translated to the Defence, and then I'm going to ask him some questions about the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the document cannot be, should not be introduced through this witness. It could be perhaps marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we have to hear from the witness, to see whether he knows anything about it. You may be a little premature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hope that it will become clear after a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I see I'm not the only person having to use Mr. Butt's statement as a fact. I have asked the court deputy to inquire into the heating system in this court. It's unduly hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, can you read the first line of the document where it says subject. What does this document pertain to?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subject? It reads, "large explosion in Hrasnica on 7th of April, 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In your team meetings with other United Nations Military Observers, do you remember this meeting being reported or spoken about?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are not the team meetings but we used to have to team leaders meetings periodically in our headquarters where team leaders of UNMO's team from both the side would attend along with senior military observer and his staff giving the overall view of the situation, then to various sectors, and in team-wise detail. And I do remember that this kind of explosion was referred in one of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P224, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I now show the witness 65 ter 02279. I'm sorry, I apologise to the court deputy. I actually mean 65 ter 2283, but I will be using this one next. I'm sorry. Can the English version be zoomed up a little bit? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, on your left-hand side of the screen, do you see a document there, firstly?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And on the top left-hand corner of the document do you see it written there the "SRK, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps Command, strictly confidential, number 20/04-1-103, 7 April 1995." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we recently had a document that was shown to the witness and he had some knowledge about it, but I don't understand how he can be shown a document that he knows absolutely nothing about. And he can't know anything about it. I don't know what about happen to this document later. It may possibly be marked for identification, but he cannot know anything about this document. Maybe the Prosecutor can explain himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Here again, we must await the questions an answers. I won't pre-determine the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Actually, can the second page be zoomed in just a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, is that page readable to you?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you see where it says, number 2, "our forces"?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And given that you have read the top left-hand corner of the first page, that this document came from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, would the reference to "our forces" refer to the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see in -- you see it says, "We responded to enemy fire as follows," and then there are two sentences. I want you to concentrate on the second sentence. Do you see that there, where it says,"In Ilidza, one 122-millimetre mine was fired, and one 250 KG AB aerial bomb was launched at the centre of Hrasnica." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it is clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is this reference to the firing of a 250 kilogramme aerial bomb at the centre of Hrasnica appear to you to be the incident that you saw on the previous document and discussed at your team leader meeting?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the face of it, it does appear to have a connection with the previous letter and, sure, some connection with that incident reported in that report, which was later subsequently discussed in our team leaders's meeting at PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the date there, 7 April 1995, at the top?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. Third line on the left top corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is the date 7 April 1995 the same date that was on the UN report that we saw a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I recall correctly in that it was the incident took place in the morning, whereas the timings are also given in this report and those are of 1700 hours of 7th April. In the fourth line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the forth line says, "Regular combat report. The situation at 1700 hours." In other words, does this report refer to the events on that day, that is the 7th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President I would like to offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P225, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply can't understand the-- what the Prosecutor suggested is possible. On several similar occasions yesterday, when the witness was much more qualified to comment on certain documents, the decision was to mark them for identification, whereas now the Prosecutor wants to tender this into evidence in the same way as the earlier document about which the witness said what he said and on this one he can't even authenticate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, there is a big difference between what you sought to do yesterday and what the Prosecutor is doing today. Yesterday, all that the witness whom you questioned was able to do was to confirm that you had correctly read what was in the statement. Today, this witness is going further. He's confirming the substance, the contents of the statement, and that is why he can tender it into evidence. You simply read from the document and asked the witness to confirm what you said, and the witness did that. The witness never confirmed the substance of the statement. And evidently he was not in a position to. This witness is confirming the contents of the statement, and that is the significant difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me just add one more thing. The witness that I examined yesterday was a policeman, and I examined him in the context of his knowledge or lack of knowledge that the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina shot at their own people. It was only in that context. I accepted your decision to that have marked for identification, only because there will be easily another 50 or so witnesses who will be able to speak about that. I agree that this document, too, be marked for identification. Of course, it is up to you and if you decide to exhibit it immediately, that's all can I say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber has given its ruling. Please proceed. The time for the break. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue. How much longer will be you, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have about five minutes. I want to show one more document and then I will be finished. I would just lying to mention one thing before I continue; that is, the court registrar has informed me that the UN document, the handwritten UN document that was tendered, was within a range of 250 pages, and, apparently, that range has in the process of it being admitted -- has been admitted as well. And there are only select pages that I want to tender into evidence. So I would just like to correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So that would be 65 ter 2341, that would be pages 49 to 58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, could I just be reassured that 65 ter document 2341 is actually on your exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we were given the document only yesterday, and we should have been given the document 48 hours in advance, in view of the volume of the document. We received the document only yesterday. Now, this document that we did not have occasion to read is being exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What do you say to that, Mr. Sachdeva?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly, the exhibit is 2341 and it is indeed on our exhibit list. And, secondly, my case manager has informed me that it has been on the list that we are ordered to provide to the Defence within the correct time period. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is where, at the beginning of the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Prior to the beginning -- yes, before the start of the examination-in-chief. It is correct that a translation is not at this time available and is being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, what are the pages to be translated, the specific pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The pages to be translated are 49 to 58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation is not an issue here. My team do speak English. The point of the matter is that we did not receive it either in English or a translation of it. We received the document only yesterday, and we were able to look at the document only yesterday when we left court. That is the issue: We didn't have either the English or the translation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How many pages are in this document? I think you told us earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Pages 49 to 58. That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. How many pages in the document in its entirety. I'm addressing the question raised by Mr. Tapuskovic, that you did not adhere to the timetable of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can explain, Mr. President. The document that I'm seeking to tender or that has been admitted, the pages that I want are nine pages within a huge range of other pages, other documents, which are difficult documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. That is a different issue from the one raised by Mr. Tapuskovic. Because when you would have passed on the document to him as required, you wouldn't have identified nine pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You identified the nine pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The Prosecution did identify the nine pages. An e-mail was sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was that done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: 9.56, in the morning, on the 13th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If the document is over 100 pages -- if it's over 100 pages, 72 hours notice is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I'm allowed to. With your leave, I have the e-mail open, and it is sent from my case manager to the Defence case manager and learned counsel, both counsel. That's exhibit 2341, pages -- and I indicate the pages by stating the ERN; in other words, I say ZAO 25135 to ZAO 25144, which is nine pages, and that is marked in bold for the benefit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it would seem, Mr. Tapuskovic, that the Prosecutor compiled with the disclosure requirements for the exhibit. Now the -- you are identifying the pages now for translation. Let us now move on quickly. Have you identified the pages for translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, pages 49 to 58 of that range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Pages 48 to 58. Yes, thank you. It's still very hot here. If the court deputy -- were you able address that issue of the temperature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, your cross-examination. You're not finished? I'm sorry. You're on your feet to take a point?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honours, I have been able to overcome these matters so far. On the eve of examination-in-chief, we receive -- or have been receiving thousands of pages, not the hundreds much pages. That was the case recently. I have to tell you that we have received these documents. We normally receive them all in a batch. That is why I cannot really confirm whether we received it or not. But just before a witness takes the stand, we receive thousands of documents, and that was the case with Mr. Butt here, that we received all these documents a day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, the Prosecutor has provided us with sufficient information to satisfy us that the document was transmitted to you in good time. Now, you must ensure that you can receive it. You have a case manager. Please proceed, and let's conclude your examination-in-chief. This has been going on too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Can document 65 ter 2279 be brought up, please. Can the English translation be zoomed in a bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, do you see a document, an English document on the left-hand side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see on the left hand side that is says SRK, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, Strictly Confidential, Number 20/04-118, 6 April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see that on the next line, it is addressed to the Ilidza Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And under the title, "Order," if you see that there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, in asking the witnesses about this document, you are not to lead him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm speaking prospectively. I'm not saying that you have done that. But you have to elicit the information that you want from him without leading him, because these are contentious issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I was not under the impression that I had not led him, but I take you for that advice on board. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry, can the document be brought back? I don't know if it's been zoomed in too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, do you see under point 1? Do you see point 1 there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that under order written in bold letters, paragraph 1, which reads, "The Ilidza Brigade will immediately prepare a launcher with an aerial bomb and transport the bomb for launching. The most" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will not be explaining myself in detail. But as a matter of principle, I believe that within the spirit of the rules, this is absolutely impermissible, but it is up to you of course to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you haven't heard the question, Mr. Tapuskovic. You have not heard the question. You haven't heard Guard the answer. How can you say it's impermissible? That is entirely illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if documents are going to be introduced in this way where the witness, upon hearing something being read out to him in a leading way, will be expected to comment on matters that are -- he is not relevant to comment upon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, merely reading out what paragraph 1 says is not leading. It is the next question that may be leading. All he was doing is what you did yesterday, which in your case was only marked for identification. He asking him, Have you seen paragraph 1 where it says that the Ilidza Brigade will immediately prepare to launch a rocket," et cetera. And he says, Yes. That doesn't take us any further. It is the next question which will go to the content, the substance of it. So please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, after that, on the next line -- well, can you read the next line, starting from "the most profitable target?"

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The most profitable target must be selected in Hrasnica or Sokolovic Kolonija, where the greatest casualties and material damage would be inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The first question I want the to ask you is given your military experience, what does that last sentence imply to you? What is this the order about?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is about two things; one is to prepare the aerial bomb and be selected, use against the most profitably selected target where greatest maximum casualties -- casualties and material damage could be inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see the reference there to Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hrasnica or Sokolovic colonies are residential areas have been mentioned which are normally at that time civilian target.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the reference to Hrasnica, is that the same place where the -- the same place where the UN report related to, the incident that the UN report discusses, is that in the same place?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two things evident from this letter. Number one, locality Hrasnica and Sokolovic have been referred in this; whereas, in the previous letter which was shown to me, referred to only Hrasnica. However, Hrasnica has also been referred to here. Number two, these are the general locations; but keeping in mind that timings and date of both letters, they do have relevance and connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in your view as a military person, the previous document from the 7th of April, 1995 that emanated from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps where it reported that its own forces had hit targets in Hrasnica on the 7th of April, does there appear to you to be a connection between that document and this one on the 6th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as I mentioned earlier, on the face of it, it appears to have a strong connection between all of these documents which have been being shown; time-wise, date-wise, and addresses-wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P226, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is the examination-in-chief, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Tapuskovic, your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I'm Defence counsel for the accused, General Milosevic. I here you were born on the 27th of September, 1957; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I myself was born on the 27th of September, but in some other year, so I suppose that this might facilitate our communication in some way. Could you, first, show the Trial Chamber on the map behind you the location of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
