utterances.text: Do you know where the tunnel was -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you have asked him to do one thing. Let him do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Sarajevo, and the scale is too small. This is the airport which was on the western side of Sarajevo city. It was further west where -- west and up this Hrasnica, and because -- I really can't see. It's so small. If I could be given some large shall map, I can point on that. It is only Sarajevo I can see. This is a small little place. If this is the north, It should be...

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us where the airport was on this map, Butmir Airport. You must be very familiar with that. You spent a year there. Where the airport is where the UN forces were stations?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Airport and which UN forces, sir? Because there were quite a few forces in Sarajevo. So airport, I have understood. I will point out that on the map. Other than that, if you could be very specific about the UN forces, only then I will be point out. Otherwise, it will take some time. And a little larger map where I can point out various locations of battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Sir, I'm only interested in knowing -- or rather, in you showing us where the airport is on the map. I'm not interested in knowing where each of the individual battalions were stationed.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, sir. I show you the airport and Hrasnica. This is Sarajevo, and now the scale is so small. It was on the west towards the airport at the end of the main road, which is not really visible here. And further west was the Hrasnica, across the airport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, twice now the witness has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I was just going to that say twice now the witness has complained about the scale of the map; in other words, it's difficult for him to mark precisely where counsel has asked him to mark. I wonder if a more appropriate map could be used for this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has difficulty identifying it precisely because of the scale of the map, Mr. Tapuskovic. You heard him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: My colleague has a smaller map here. Please pass that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a United Nations map, or rather, UNPROFOR map. Can you show us where the airport is on that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, the Chamber just passed a map to him. Now, let him try with that map first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the airport, Sarajevo airport, this is the Butmir area, and this was the Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now show us the location of the airport on this large map, after having seen it on the small one?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be difficult, but, you see, it is so small. It is not possible to point out here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, you said that Hrasnica was on this side of the tunnel. Do you know about the laying down of the tunnel between the downtown Sarajevo and which actually went underneath the airport?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have knowledge of that tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: See, Hrasnica is at the exit of the tunnel. As you pass the airport, you first reach Hrasnica, and you can see it clearly on the map. Take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as existence of tunnel is concerned, it is true it was there. I had seen the exit towards the west -- west -- south of airport landing strip, little far away, but it was not in the centre of Hrasnica. It was a little before Hrasnica while going from Sarajevo to Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That is indeed the case. Can you tell us roughly how far from the exit of the tunnel is Hrasnica, on the road to Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the distance because this was not actually my area of responsibility. However, it was quite far, that is Hrasnica from the exit of the tunnel which was towards the south-west of the airport, the landing strip itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: According to the map scale, can you roughly tell the distance? You were not able to locate it on the large map. But on the small map, when you look at the scale in centimetres, could you convert it into metres and tell us roughly what the distance was between the tunnel and Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a sizeable distance which could be mixed up with the exit of tunnel, which we are referring to, and the locality of Hrasnica. The distance I may not be able to, because this was not my area of responsibility, as I have been very specific in my area of responsibility. It was some other team, so they could have been asked about it. It is not possible for me to remember after 12 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That is quite understandable. You were located elsewhere at Mali Hum. We will deal with that later. Can you confirm that the UNPROFOR forces and all the other forces in control in Sarajevo were able to see, on a daily basis, troops entering the tunnel and exiting it going in different directions? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as tunnel is concerned, I am very much aware of it and I do confirm it. But its usage and whether UNPROFOR was able to see the incoming or outgoing troops, since it was in my area of responsibility, so I really can't comment. Because I was neither -- had any kind of observation of that area, nor I had any UNMO there. So it is really difficult for me to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have one other question in relation to this. Are you aware that the Hrasnica area, at the time you were there in particular, was completely free of civilian population because the civilian population could get in harm's way when the army was passing through? Were you aware of this on the basis of the information the UNPROFOR had at the time, that the area was a military target and as was therefore completely civilian-free?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. During my area of tenure with the United Nations Military Observer mission in Sarajevo, once I visited, let's be very specific, the next day once this -- this Hrasnica was hit by aerial bomb, a couple of UNMOs were hurt. I have already made reference in the earlier part of the examination or statement. People from the locality, the civilians, had gathered around us and were asking to get the blue flag away from the building and also relocate the team, as this was attracting fire. And it was previously also -- it had also previously happened, and later on this was one of the main reason to relocate the team, and those all were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago when answering the questions put by my learned friend, you spoke of Hrasnica in great detail. Do you know what the situation there Hrasnica was at the entrance to the tunnel? Were you aware of any military operations going on there at the time? How were you able to answer the Prosecutor's questions about this?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to answer those question because I was made president of the investigation, though it was not my area of responsibility. Once that team suffered damages, next day, that was 2nd of July, I went there and carried out investigation. That's why I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what did the investigation establish? Did you determine the existence of any casualties, were any civilians hurt, how many, or maybe a soldier was killed?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there were, first of all, a couple of UNMOs hurt. One of them, Major Ejas [phoen] was hospitalised, and I very clearly remember there were, I was told, a few civilian casualties. And out of them, few were transported in one of the UNMO's vehicle. If I remember correctly and definitely, there were civilian casualties along with the UNMOs. And when I say UNMOs, I refer to the persons and to the material. One of vehicle, United Nations, was totally damaged. Other armoured vehicle was severely damaged but it could still run and the generator was off. And accommodations where these UNMOs were living, having blue flag on its top duly illuminated, also was subject to severe damages, as was the case in the surrounding buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, that was something that you heard from others, but what did you establish on the spot when you came there the next day?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the things which we examined on the site did support this viewpoint which I have given if my previous answer to your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more thing. In all those months, did you see that air bomb flying through the air?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw any air bomb flying with my own eyes or through the binoculars. I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you claim that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was not in possession of such bombs, I mean air bombs.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had not seen any air bomb travelling, as far as Serbs are concerned, in the air, so I say I didn't see that. Now as far as Bosnian are concerned, whether they were in possession of such weapon, I had never seen any weapon in my area of responsibility or discussed in any of team leader's meeting that there was some speculation even of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago when you were examined by the Prosecutor, you discussed one document, although it was a document that you had dealt with on your job, which is understandable. I, however, would like to show you something emanating from the military staff of military observers. It's D31. It's a report from the Sector Sarajevo. I'm not going to bother you with those bombs again, but I do want you to have a look at this document. Do you see, sir, this report, which is on your screen now? It is an allegation in the indictment that the building of the television was hit on that day by an air bomb of this kind. Now, read it for yourself. This special report speaks about the impact of a projectile on the television building in June 1995. And it says that this high ranking officer of the UNMO saw the projectile flying over the parking lot and the street from a certain coordinate, and we see in brackets that the places on BiH territory approximately 1800 metres from the nearest cease-fire line. So the claim made here is that the Bosnian side fired the projectile in question. My question is: Did you ever discuss this document at some important meeting, or have you ever heard or seen this document?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, let me confirm for you that this appears to be a valid document, because the name reflected against, prepared by, and released by, I know both the gentlemen. Their tenure overlap with my tenure with the United Nations in Sarajevo. However, I do not confirm that any incident where BiH was alleged to have used as has been mentioned in this document, which being shown to me, was ever discussed in the team leaders' meeting which used to be held. And this gentleman, Colonel Alam, from Bangladesh, though it was not shown here. And Hansen, he was an operation officer, Captain Hansen. He was also there. I don't remember if it was ever discussed in any of the team leaders' meeting, which was the right forum we used share. We used to get the briefings from both of these gentlemen, including the senior military observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, maybe it was a very confidential document, maybe it was secret to some extent, and maybe that is the reason why it perhaps did not reach your team leaders' meetings. Could that be a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, let's be very clear. It is addressed to UNMO, UNPROFOR Headquarters Sarajevo and UNMO Headquarters at Zagreb. It has,- as far as this paper is concerned, nothing to do with my team. It was not supposed to reach to me. However, in the subsequent team leader meeting, it was supposed to be discussed, briefing was to be given. All those incidents or such-like incidents used to be covered in those meetings in detail, and everybody used to give his input. And for the entire theatre with special focus on Sarajevo, we used to get the briefings and details of various incidents. And I thought if -- I don't know. This was, at least I never heard anything it, in any the team leaders' meetings which I was attended, and I also there, roughly, the date when this letter was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Which is -- what is the date of the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Date is 29th June, sir, 1230 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 29th June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was roughly the time I was there. I was still -- 29th August, I was in charge of my team and then I handed over this team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, where is Captain Hansen and Lieutenant-Colonel Alam? Are they on your witness list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Alam is not on our witness list; and if I recall correctly, Mr. President, you asked me a similar question a couple of days, and I informed the Court that Mr. Hansen was on our witness list but he is not anymore. He was dropped when we made the amendment to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Are you proposing to endeavour to call these two officers as witnesses, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think it would be within my capacity. I have to explain to you. We are only four on our team working on this. I believe the Trial Chamber should within their own authority call these witnesses, because I don't have the organizational capacity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We can call them, but how can you say you don't have the organisational capacity? I don't accept that. This is crucial evidence for the Defence. It would completely destroy one plank of the Prosecution's case. If you don't call these witnesses, the Chamber will call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, might I add one thing. We have contacted Mr. Hansen, and we are endeavouring to find the identity of the UNMO that is, you know, the subject of this report, the UNMO who allegedly witnessed this -- this projectile flying, and so with we're endeavouring to do that to assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm again faced with a problem. Maybe I will have to show you this map again, although I believe that the larger one is more convenient. You said your positions were at Mali Hum; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. It was at Mali Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This Mali Hum, is it a little below what is called Veliki Hum, which is over 800 metres tall?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am given the chance to show my exact position at Mali Hum on the previous map, which was used to point out Hrasnica and the airport, I submit to Your Honour, sir, that might help me and to point out my position, sir, if I'm permitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I think we should see the upper part better.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- these are the two ends towards north-east; the one which is towards south, that was about 50 yards from this point, towards south-west was our accommodation. It was Vrnici [phoen] Street, and I also remember its number, 49G. Mr. Abid was its owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that place -- no, you can't on this map. How far from there --

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very much clear. I can show that, yes. It is very much clear. I can point out. I have pointed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, yes. [Interpretation] Can you tell us the elevation of that spot? You are a soldier. What was the altitude of Mali Hum?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The altitude I don't remember, but it should be about 6.000 -- roughly somewhere, a little plus or minus, 6.000 feet where we were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You are speaking in feet. How much could that be in metres.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to consult, sir, my calculator. It may not be possible for me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Divide by 39 inches, I think. I think it is three feet, three inches.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very poor at mathematics. I never liked figures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I have been-- Roughly, I can see it was a little less than 6.000 feet, becomes a little less than 2.000 metres. It is a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard 6.000 metres. That is impossible.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 6.000 feet, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, yes. [Interpretation] Please, what about Veliki Hum? How far was the top of this hill called Veliki Hum? How far was it from you, and how much higher was it?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the top of it was some telecom or some communication huge tower. It was about four, five minutes walk with two turns, only about three to -- about 300 yards from our accommodation. And that was the top where that tower was located, and it is also shown on this map also. Where this winding road ends, next to that is that tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On that tower and on that entire hill there were units of the ABiH stationed. Is it correct that the ABiH army took up positions on that hill?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no BiH positions. However, on that tower in the compound or the premises of the tower, there were a few soldiers present with their weapons; those were rifles, et cetera. About five, seven, they used to remain there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: To the left, as I see here, there's another hill, Zuc, 830 metres high; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From Mali Hum and from Zuc, is it the case that you see Sarajevo as in the palm of your hand?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember from the Zuc because that was not, sir, my area of responsibility. As far as Mali Hum is concerned, you are very right, it was just like palm of your hand. You could see the Sarajevo, especially starting from Skenderija and going across Skenderija, Jewish cemetery, chapel, red building, Vrbanja bridge, and Tito barracks. That is all you could see. And very clearly, you could see and Debelo Brdo also, I may add.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning Zuc, I don't want to ask you anything except for this. Do you know that on that mountain, Zuc, there were units of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I don't remember, because, as I have already mentioned, it was not my area of responsibility. And about the meetings, I really do not remember. It would not be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From that line, from those two spots but primarily the spot you were on, all the way until the end of that yellow line depicting the area of responsibility of the BiH army, can we say that it was all under the control of the BiH army and that at this point the slope begins and there are no longer any members of the army of Republika Srpska, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slopes towards the city from Zuc are Mali Hum. The slopes, I make clear those towards the assault of Zuc top and Mali Hum top, up hill Miljacka river, in between area was under BiH control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you did not understand me. You have already explained that bit. But I am interested in the direction towards the north. From those hills, you control this slope all the way up to the yellow line that depicts the positions of the BiH army; is that correct? From Zuc and from here, the slope goes down toward this is yellow line. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But again this is not within the purview of my responsibility. It was not my area of responsibility. It was towards the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that perfectly. I just want you to explain what you were able to see from your position, and you have done that. Do you know that behind this red line in this depression, there is a place called Vogosca. Have you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Out of all this material I received two days ago, I would like to show you one document, on which I would like to ask you then a military question. And I will throughout be trying to present documents of an impartial party; namely the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is 65 ter DD00-478, a report by General Janvier to Kofi Annan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please have a look. "The staff of the peace force of the United Nations in Zagreb, Urgent, for United Nations." Is that what is written here?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Immediate unrestricted joint operation centre GT land operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] "22nd August 1995 at 1900 hours, Lieutenant-General Janvier, the commander of the UN force, writes directly to Kofi Annan, Secretary-General of the United Nations." Did I read this correctly?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now find the heading "Sector Sarajevo" in this document. It's already on the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You see "UNPROFOR, Sector Sarajevo"? I'd like to read to you -- "Sector Sarajevo," do you see this subheading.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do see. Sir, I do see. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it to you. "Sector Sarajevo: The BiH side fired eight rounds at 0900 hours and six rounds at 1250 hours at the Bosnian Serb side. The Bosnian Serb side responded with 30 shells into the town in Sedrenik." Is that written there?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it started not with the eight rounds, it starts with "a factory, GR," which stands, as I understand, for grid reference in bracket, "grid reference 885645 in Vogosca in BSA side was shelled with eight rounds at 0900 Bravo and six rounds at 1250 Bravo," and Bravo is for B. "Grid reference BP 914613." Yes, I can read, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, it is a catastrophe of the translation. "Sector Sarajevo: The Bosnian-Herzegovina side fired eight rounds at 0900 and six rounds at 1250 at a factory Vogosca." Is that written correctly.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then the Bosnian Serb side, as I read a moment ago, responded with fire.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thirty shells, they responded with. Yes, it is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Have you ever seen this before? Was this ever shown to your units because you were precisely----

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I have also made a mention that such-like documents, which were addressed to senior headquarters, were not shown to us. But notice in the subsequent team leaders' meetings, such-like incidents were always addressed and reported and briefed. And if this is the incident which happened, which I don't remember because it was not related to my area after 12 years, it must have also been reported in the team leaders' meeting, if it has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this was strictly confidential. Can I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. There was nothing confidential. In the team leaders' meetings, we used to have all available information. We used to be briefed by the concerned staff officers and the senior observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, several days ago, General Nicolai testified here, who was man number two in NATO during your time there. There was some other witnesses, too. I wasn't counting the amount of shells. But when I asked General Nicolai, and I will read to you what it is that I asked him. "Yesterday, you said, didn't you, that it was necessary to fire several shells to hit a target. You cannot fire only one and be sure that you have hit the target, unless of course the shooting or the shelling is random. Did I understand you well? You said yes, in reply to that." And then General Nicolai's answer was: "Yes, you understood me well. Where there's a significant amount of shells fired, you have to fire a proportionate number of shells in response to that." Is that your position as well as an officer?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the proficiency of the gunners, whosoever it operating those weapons or guns, that how quickly if they are really interest today engage, the specific target can engage. It depends on many things everything. It the might take two or three shells or four or five. It depends. So this is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the case we were discussing a moment ago, the BiH army fired 14 shells and the other side fired 30 shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, of course, I have no objection to this line of questioning. But if we are referring to the incident as recorded in this UN document, then it should be stated that the -- the eight rounds fired by the Bosnian army were fired at a factory, and that's what is recorded here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it fired eight rounds at 9.00 and six rounds at 1250, 14 rounds in all. And I believe the sum total is quite simple to arrive at. I don't see the point of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The point being made was that the rounds were fired at a factory, which is what it says in the English translation at any rate. A factory in Vogosca in ABiH side was shelled with eight rounds and six rounds by BiH. And the Prosecutor attaches some importance to the -- to the to the target being a factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my translation into B/C/S, the difference is only in the time. At 9.00 there were eight rounds, and at 1250 there were six rounds. So in an interval of six hours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Three hours--

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- there were two times during which rounds were fired, 14 in all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not the point. It's the target. Are you saying that the B/C/S doesn't have reference to the target being a factory? Is that not in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, of course. I highlighted in particular and that factory is in the centre of Vogosca. Please, don't you know that this in the centre of an inhabited area. Are you aware of this? The factory in Vogosca is surrounded by civilian buildings, and even a factory is a civilian building where civilians are employed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It depends on the factory, doesn't it. But you must put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, a factory was targeted. I may even concede that was used for some war purposes. But that is it was surrounded by war buildings is something that is beyond any doubt. There were civilians living in their homes, and this is what I'm asking you: Are you aware of this? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir. In the capacity of the a military officer with 29 and a half years experience, I would submit, Your Honour, sir, if it was of some kind of defence material producing factory, it was a legible target. The factory, itself, whether it was some kind of ordnance, ordnance being produced there or some weaponry or some other material which was being used in the field, yes, to my mind it was a legitimate target, only the premises of that factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That may be so, General. But the question you're being asked is whether the factory is in the centre of Vogosca, and whether you know that this is in the centre of an inhabited area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The factory is surrounded by civilian buildings. Can you confirm that or comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, since it was under the control of BSA, under Serb control, I never visited Vogosca, so I can't confirm, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I told you what General Nicolai said. That was his position. I'm asking you the following: First, eight rounds were fired and then probably the Serb side responded; and then a further six rounds were fired and the Serbian side responded. We heard what General Nicolai had to say about that. I'd like to know what your opinion is. Was the return fire appropriate? Was it something that the Serb side was compelled to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was consulting with my brother. But your last questions, it seems to me, is certainly not something he could answer, whether it was something that the Serb side was compelled to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do believe that several days ago we discussed the matter. The Trial Chamber believed that the witness may say something about the proportionality and criteria to be governed by my question was to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, not as it came across. The last question, "Was it something that the Serb side was compelled to do," would not be appropriate. The one before, "Was the return fire appropriate."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So that would be -- that would be an appropriate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I am not insisting on the witness giving his opinion. If he wishes to, he may.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to tell us anything about this, having heard what General Nicolai had to say with regard to the incident. You heard that the fire was first opened at 0900 and probably there was return fire; whereupon, there was fire opened at 1250 again. Can you tell us anything about that, having regard to what His Honour Judge Robinson just said.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, sir, with the -- my experience and background, to my mind, it is a routine that military targets, and I repeat, the military targets quite frequently and as per routine are softened up. We used term "softening of the targets." We measure in the morning and we measure in the afternoon, maybe in the evening and at night. It depends upon the potency of the target, and this is for military target. But in this very paragraph, the response what I read from the Serb side has been on the towns of Sedrenik and there was something else. I don't know. But as far as whether it was from the ABiH side, and if that factory was a military purpose factory, whether it was twice or three times or four times, it is very much legitimate. It is against a military target, and they can resort it for ten days. It is very common, and it is a military practice. Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Lest I should forget, although I do not have many questions left, during your time there, one of the commanders in UNPROFOR was General Rose; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that based on what some other witness said, Mr. Harland, who has yet to testify, and based on a document, there was mention of the members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina shooting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did you say that Mr. Harland has yet to testify? Because that is what is on the transcript. Mr. Harland has testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Has the witness heard General Rose saying that Muslims often opened fire on their own people? Did General Rose ever say anything to that effect at any of their meetings together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- that question needs to be backed up by some reference, some quote; otherwise, it's -- I don't know on what basis he is saying that General Rose said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at any rate, General Rose will be called here; and in view of the objection raised, I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, several days ago, we heard a statement made by General Fraser in this courtroom. But before that, let me ask you this: You were in Sarajevo during the events in the summer of 1995. Yes or no. I believe you did testify to that effect when answering the Prosecutor's questions. You know that in these events in Sarajevo many people were killed, including civilians and soldiers. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which side, sir? You want to ask me about Serb side or Sarajevo side -- or BiH side or both sides?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you did not go often to the Serb side, I'm asking you about the people who got killed in Sarajevo. Can you confirm to me that the offensive of the 15th of June was launched by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't confirm that 15th June offensive was launched by Bosnia-Herzegovina, no. Because if I remember correctly, this is in reference to the date, I say again the date, if I remember correctly, on 7th June, Serb attacked Debelo Brdo and Jewish cemetery area. But their firing was not restricted only to those bunkers and ABiH positions. It was all over the Sarajevo. And I may make a mention here, since we were experiencing UNMOs on the Lima side, Lima side is the Serb side. From 11th of May onward, they had severe restriction of movement; and when I restriction of movement, they were not supposed to go out of their accommodations and to conduct any to patrolling on any occasion. I also remember on 6th of June, we had team leaders' meetings and team leaders from the Lima side, which was supposed to attend the meetings at headquarters, were not allowed even to come to the BiH side to the headquarters to attend that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. You were asked about the offensive on the 15th of June, and you're dealing with an earlier date now. Are you leading up to the 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm coming to that. And because from our observation post, especially area I'm referring to, Barracks Boset west of Jewish cemetery, the preparations were there and the last signal was stopping UNMOs of the Lima side to attend teem leaders' meeting. And in that meeting, since we were observing the preparations in this area from three, four days, I did make a mention that Serb attack was imminent on -- within next 72 hours and it was taken on record. Unfortunately, very next day, there was attack. And subsequently on 15th of June, there was again shelling, but I don't know specifically on 15th of June who start the attack. It is not to my knowledge. I just wanted to link up. Because on Serb side there was complete restriction of movement, and on our side we were not allowed to meet our UNMOs to share what is going on. All that we could observe, we did report and did share in team leaders' meeting, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I will never interrupt your answers, although you should have, first, answered my question and then engaged in additional explanations. I would like to know whether Debelo Brdo was occupied by strong forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You were mentioning bunkers and so on and so forth. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Debelo Brdo, on the BiH side, there were two strong bunkers or the positions, which were occupied by the BiH, and I do confirm that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You, as an officer, can you tell us whether deep inside the area of responsibility of army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, once you passed the front line, how far into the area of responsibility, how far behind the confrontation line were the units of army of Bosnia and Herzegovina positioned, and also how far behind the confrontation line were the units of the Serbian army positioned, based on your knowledge at the time?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, coming to your question, sir, straight way, first, let's understand that this was not classical war going on. These were not the conventional armies. These were the two warring factions. Their organisations, which I know of the BiH side and a little bit through team leaders' meeting I also have knowledge about BSA side. These were not the conventional units, the fighting units. So talking about in classical military sense, the depth, the reserves, that aspect was probably missing in that. In classical military sense, a battle is going on. How can you have at 50 yards, a main road being used by the civilian for their daily earning, commuters passing by. On both sides, civilians were there, only 20, 30 feet away from the confrontation line, and those houses, residential areas on both sides were occupied. So, first of all, we have to, sir, remember that it is not classical sense in that we have screens, then we have mobile troops, then we have that position, and then the reserves. Sir, it was not the case here. It was the confrontation line and some locations where they had few high-calibre weapons deployed or wanted to deploy, so it was all. It was not in classical sense having that in that, sir

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: One senior UN officer, namely General Fraser, do you know that the Presidency building was in the centre of Sarajevo? Was it a military target? A couple of days ago, General Fraser said, and I will try to quote him as faithfully as possible. Although the Supreme Command was in the centre of Sarajevo throughout his tenure, it was never targeted. Did you ever see, also during this particular offensive regardless of who launched it, the building of the Presidency and Supreme Command directly targeted by the members of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, to my mind, I must submit to the Honourable Court that civilian president, the civilian government, the political government, they cannot be legitimately labeled as military target. Commander in chief and downward and all the ordnance factories and the troops are legitimate target. Number one, sir. Now, coming over to the Presidency, yes, you are right, that at least during my tenure of duty, there was not any direct hit which comes to my mind. But very close to that, very close to that, the pavement next to the Presidency, on the corner where the small road with [indiscernible] where the Zulu restaurant was, one night there was shelling and there were casualties. I do confirm. But you are right, sir, during my tenure, I don't have anything in my mind that the Presidency was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: General Fraser categorically claimed that never, during his term of office there, did this take place. And I will find this, should the Prosecution object or for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, that the command the -- or the President of the Presidency the Supreme Commander were never targeted. And let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He has already agreed, so let's move on. He said it never happened during his tenure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, I wanted to ask you something else concerning the shooting in general. You say that the fire was opened only upon Sarajevo. Was there any return fire out of Sarajevo by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Was there any outgoing fire from downtown Sarajevo aimed at the army of Republika Srpska; and if so, to what extent? What was its volume?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was fire on the confrontation line between the two positions and that means from the BiH side, the military firing from the confrontation line. During attacks ... Sir, let me reflect, and I want to make a mention. If I remember correctly, there were four or five major attacks. And in those days, there was some shelling to the military targets from the north of Mali Hum tower. I do confirm. And this was from the BiH. But I cannot confirm whether it was on the civilian side, because I was not on that side. But there was definitely, during those attacks, it came from the reverse of my slope where I was on the other side towards the north. And if you want -- the Honourable Court want, I can generally -- I don't remember that because I had not seen the exact locations. I can give the general locality from where the fire came and that it went towards the BSA side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, ten days before you, we heard another witness, Mohatarem, who was a high-ranking representative of an international organisation. He spoke a lot about possible military targets. And when he spoke of the depth of the front line, he said that it was reckoned to be two kilometres from the confrontation or demarcation line, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No doubt, you have a point to make about citation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, precisely. And this basically covers the other witnesses that my learned friend has mentioned today. Of course, it's not a problem for counsel to do that. But just in the in order to be accurate, if he's going to do that, then perhaps a reference or references could be given. If indeed he is quoting or alleged to be quoting from the witness' evidence, then it should be recorded somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think there is a point there, Mr. Tapuskovic, certainly, if the quotation is going to be challenged. But these are all contentious matters. So you can't speak generally, you have to speak accurately. So you should come prepared with the lines from the transcript to which we may refer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understand perfectly well what you are saying and I understand my colleague's objection, but I absolutely stand by the words that I have just uttered.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It occurred to me just this moment, and if I were forced to look now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, what precisely are you saying is incorrect in what Mr. Tapuskovic put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not saying that anything is indeed incorrect, and I'm not at any rate trying to cast aspersions on my learned friend at all in that regard. All I'm saying is that as we had an experience today with a written document in front of our eyes where the points about the factory not mentioned in the question. It's just so we can be sure that if the witness's evidence is being quoted, I could be given a reference. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think it very much depends on the context. I wouldn't not want to lay it on a hard-and fast rule. It depends on the particular circumstances, but here I will allow the questioning to continue. But bear in mind, Mr. Tapuskovic, where you're going to refer to evidence, it may be necessary on occasions to have a specific reference to the particular line in the transcript, so that it may be verified, if challenged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're perfectly right and you've cautioned me about it earlier, and I did prepare some references concerning the evidence of General Nicolai, but this point just occurred to me at this moment. I don't have anything prepared concerning the evidence of Mr. Mohatarem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me what is the depth of the front line, judging purely by the general principles of military science.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in case of conventional armies, at battalion level in conventional army, that could be 1.000 metre and it could be 1.500 metres depending on the area and the strength of the battalion, because battalion varies from country to country. At brigade level, it may be five to eight kilometres, keeping in mind the factors I have already mentioned. At the divisional level, it may be 15 kilometres. At the corps level - the conventional corps, please remember - it may be 30, 35, 40 kilometres but depends on the size of those corps, being very much conventional army organised as per the laid out standards in the use in the world by the most modern armies. And this is for the defence, not for the attack, in our case, both of the warring factions, not the regular armies. So their depth really cannot be given, because at 50 yards, as I have already quoted, on the roads civilians were living; there were schools; maybe 400 metre 500 metre, Presidency; there was a hospital on both the sides. I'm making such-like things were there, so that rule may not be applied here. However, I have given the depth in various levels, but it is true for warfare, convention, and regular armies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During those fierce offensives, and I'm not going to deal with who started it, you know very well that none of the armies at this confrontation line actually fired from the line. Are you aware of that.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Nor did either of the armies fire at the line, because they would have been killing their own troops with their own weapons. Is that also true?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true, then, that it was only possible to fire from the rear from artillery behind the lines? Is it true for both of these armies?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is true for both of the armies, and this was the very reason. In my earlier answer to your question, sir, I merely mention a few weapons firing from north of communication tower and Mali Hum, and that was reported to our headquarters. It was in one of the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were in Sarajevo and you were following these events from your observation post; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This area that you were observing and in the zone of that front line, if the civilians had been removed from that area, is it the case that there would be no casualties among civilians?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that if civilians were removed. I understand I'm a witness. I can't ask questions. But one thing I can confirm, civilians were not removed. They were living in their houses or the flats, accommodations. And whether they were -- why they were not removed, I can't comment, because I may ask you a question which probably I'm not supposed to, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'd rather you did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know very well, although you came later, that a resolution has been passed to demilitarise Sarajevo and to make it a protected area. Do you know about this resolution, and do you know whether this resolution was indeed honoured in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Generally, first of all, it was in my knowledge. It was declared demilitarised zone, but at confrontation line both the sides were present with their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But the city of Sarajevo was proclaimed a protected area, according to everything you observed. And in your belief, did the army in Sarajevo observe the spirit of that decision by ensuring that there were either no civilians around the front line or that they -- that there were no weapons or troops around the front line, in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would object with respect to the relevance of this line of questioning; in other words, the Prosecution submits that whether there was civilians in the front lines, near the front lines or not, does not impact upon the guilt or not of the accused and of the crimes alleged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what's your response to that? Explain the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is perhaps the most relevant question in the entire case. If the resolution, whose number I cannot recall now, from mid-1993 to demilitarise Sarajevo and ultimately all the other protected areas, tragedies would have been prevented. That is the most fundamental question that arises before you, and that of course you will decide upon. I know what my conviction is. But nobody can dispute the relevance of this question. At least the question, as for the decision, it is indeed yours and you will deliberate about it. If Mr. Sachdeva disputes the relevance and you decide that the witness should not answer, I will of course abide by your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, is your point that had the BH government ensured the demilitarisation of Sarajevo, then civilians would not have been killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite certainly, at least within the zone of two kilometres. That is my assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How is that relevant to the indictment? How is that relevant to the charges against the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first of all, there would have been no war anymore. There would have no conflict after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not for this Court. I won't allow the question. You haven't satisfied me as to its relevance. Please ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will come back later to those photographs. But since you almost never visited the Serb side, you only stayed in Sarajevo and observed the atrocities that happened in Sarajevo and the death of people, can you tell me were there any soldiers in Sarajevo and how many? Did you have any information as to the strength of troops in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my area of responsibility, I had two brigade headquarters looking after their troops at the confrontation line; One was 115 Brigade and one 101 Brigade. And again when I say "brigade," I will submit to the Court that these were not classical. Again, their organisation was different. These were the warring factions, not like regular army. Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that they were fighting between them?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never said that they were fighting with each other, these two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you say at all on the basis of any information you had whatsoever how many troops there were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact strength may not be possible, but I know there were -- in my area of responsibility, there were two brigade headquarters and on the confrontation line portion of the brigade, because they were defending vast area and some of the troops were deployed in other teams responsibility of area. However, their headquarters were in my area of responsibility. I used to have meetings with them, but their troops were also deployed on the confrontation line in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And according to your estimate at the time of those summer events of 1995, a significant number of people, civilians, and soldiers alike, lost their lives in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is really difficult to give the exact or even roughly estimates, but loss was too high. Every day we used to have deaths. And I'm sure on the Serb side there must also be deaths, although I didn't go to that area, but I do feel there must be deaths on that area as we were having on the BiH side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate this answer very much, because I -- it's spares me from further questioning along this line. But in that case, I have to compare this to one statement made by Mr. Fraser. He said that the rule was that Serbs abided by the principle, ten Muslims for one Serb. Mr. Fraser said this in this courtroom. Did you have such information? Did you know about something like that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is something new for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You have answered the question. Let's move on, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since that statement, this assertion was made before this Trial Chamber, I want to ask whether this myth was borne out of such events as the Markale market incident of the 28th of August, 1995, Markale II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is ridiculous. The witness has said he doesn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And does he know anything about the Markale incident? Did he have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is a different matter. You can't put a question to him based on the answer which he gave, because he denied knowing anything about it. If you want to ask him about Markale, then that is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Markale? Were you in any way involved in Markale II, an incident of the of August, 1995. Do you have any direct knowledge about that event itself? Did you investigate it, or do you have only second-hand knowledge that you received at the position you held at Mali Hum?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this locality where this sad incident took place on 28th of August, this was my second-last day in Sarajevo, or third-last day. It was not in my area of responsibility. Once this incident happened, I just passed through it. But I never conducted any investigation, so I really can't comment as far as the investigations are concerned on this very incident. Though later on I heard the details, roughly how many killed, how many injured. But it was not with them first-hand information as they never carried out or my team any kind of investigation in this specific case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I thank you for that, too. I will not asking more about that. I just want it go back to those photographs that we saw earlier today concerning an incident which you testified to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see photograph P222, and I am drawing my examination to a conclusion, but first let's see photograph P222. Can we enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butt, do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can see very much this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You marked your own location?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at this photograph, was it possible for you to be hit at that location, either from the spot which you marked as the origin of fire because there is a building in between or from any other position? Was it possible for you to be hit in view of the duration of the shooting? Can you confirm that it was in fact impossible for you to be hit either from this building or from the buildings where the ABiH army was positioned?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had narrated the whole incident during earlier questions, I do confirm. And I also confirmed in those answers of mine that from building Metalka, it was very much possible to hit me, and I did experience and heard few impacts on the snipe -- anti-sniping screen behind which I had taken cover. And the building, again I refer, has already been marked with letter M, the Metalka building. Later on I went there again, and I said it was possible. And I also saw somebody there firing at me or moving there. Now, coming over to the building which is, if we look towards Metalka building, short of river on left side, which I draw circle in the previous photograph, it was not possible, as we also visited along with the French soldiers that building to where I was hiding, even to hit the portion of screen, anti-sniping screen behind which I had taken cover. It was not possible to engage from that very building which was under BiH control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to give shorter answers in future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you were actually under cover, and I believe you. Of course, everybody would seek cover in your situation. But if you were under cover, then how were you able at that distance to see at all that for an hour and a half somebody was firing from that building, from that house, wishing to hit you? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I must ask that the transcript delete the phrase "fair enough," which has been attributed to me because I never said that. This has nothing to do with you, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So can you explain that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First, when I was in the fork-lift, I was fired upon at that instance. I saw somebody because I was already facing towards that side. And after I took cover, it was not can't use fire for one and a half hour, hour and 15 minutes. It was intermittent; sometimes they would fire a couple of rounds, sometimes a single shot. And in between, couple of times I try to peep from the sides, and I saw some movement in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's very logical and I perfectly understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see photograph P223.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you were on that side over there and when you went to look at those locations, did those buildings, held by the BiH army and especially those buildings behind, overlook or tower over the buildings held by the army of Republika Srpska? Is it obvious from this photograph? Can you answer?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, I couldn't get your question. Please, if you repeat it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The parts of these buildings that you marked with a B, that were held by the BH army, is that building taller? Does it rise above the building from which you said the shots were fired from at you? As far as I can see, one of them is certainly higher and significantly higher, but it's not up to me to say that, of course.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building which is marked with the letter R, and the portion under BiH control, these Metalka building and this very building almost of the same height. And I don't remember that it overlooked to the position where it could overlook to the position where I was taking cover near that fork-lift.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the building behind the one marked with letter B, is it higher than all the other buildings there and is it not on a hillock? Did you observe that?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is not a hillock, small little raised portion. But again the building is not that high that it could immediately overlook the building on the left of Metalka building, and also behind that is the portion of red building which was under BiH control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it possible that fire originated from there as well? And I mean the fire targeting you, if you know that the fire comes from that direction. But how can you be sure that the fire is not coming from there and not from the Metalka building? Is it possible that the fire originated in the building marked B or in the building behind it, that was also under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do confirm that building immediately behind the B portion of red building, which was under BiH control, was under BiH control. But again, we visited that area where I was, where I had taken cover. It was not visible from that -- those positions. It was not possible, because I had couple of buildings intervening in that direction. So a couple of times I saw somebody firing from Metalka building, and that I confirmed, and behind. Once I had taken cover, and I was not looking towards the building, it was only the kind of direction from where the fire was coming, and that I didn't confirm. But generally it was coming from the same direction where I was -- where I had already observed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up P88; it's a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking him to show us the spot where the French soldier was hit and to mark the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that all these high-rise buildings and sky-scrapers in particular are in the area under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, including Holiday Inn and these two other buildings. utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Holiday Inn, yes, it is it was under that the BiH control. The second building, please, if you can guide me so then I can comment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The two tallest buildings on the right-hand side, or rather, to the right of the building you have indicated, they are two sky-scrapers that do have a particular name you may have been familiar with. But they stand the tallest two buildings in the area?

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These, the dark ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark them.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] These buildings were under BiH control, this was under BiH control, this is was under BiH control, this was under BiH control, this was under BiH control, this was under BiH control. Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these places ideal for firing upon this position, if there were snipers, for firing at the place where the French soldier was hit. Were they not a more appropriate source of fire, if there were indeed armed people in these buildings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, just one question at a time. First was whether those places were ideal for firing upon that position if there were snipers. What's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, those two buildings could engage the French soldier if they were fired from that direction, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Which two buildings, because you have marked four there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These two buildings because they are taller, and they do overlook this position where French soldier was killed. It was possible that fire was fire from that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What about the yellow building? Is that the Holiday Inn.

utterances.text: Yes, sir. Again, it was very much possible. It could be engaged. It was just next to that, across the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, the second question was whether -- I'm not sure whether I got it, Mr. Tapuskovic. Whether there were not a more appropriate source of fire, more appropriate than what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. Can I put my last question.

utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: For a good marksman, was it enough to have an ordinary weapon, even a pistol, if you were in Holiday Inn in order for this man to be killed? At any rate, did it only take the most ordinary piece of weapon to kill him from there? Of course, under the proviso that there were armed people there.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, if pistol was used from Holiday Inn building, I think the distance was little more, because the range was more. So to my mind, it was not possible with ordinary pistol to kill a soldier in the fork-lift from Holiday Inn building, its site.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But even the most common of weapons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the distance between the Holiday Inn and the place where the French soldier was killed? Approximate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, it was about 75, 80 metres, 75 to 80 metres. The it's road was quite wide and the distance, and both locations were a little away from the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what was the distance between the other buildings on the right -- what was the distance between the other buildings on the right and that place where the French soldier was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, it was about 100 yards was this parliament building, the bluish one, 100, 120 yards. This was about 180 metres. This was about 250 metres from this.

utterances.text: So they were further away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were further away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's why I think Mr. Tapuskovic is asking whether from the Holiday Inn, even with the most ordinary weapon, it wouldn't be possible to kill the French soldier where he was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the rifle it was possible, but with pistol it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Effective range of pistol is about, what we consider in army, 35 to 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ASAM BUTT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly, the firing was against those two bunkers on Debelo Brdo, and these were of BiH general area, Jewish cemetery, red building. But quite a few impacts were reported and observed in the town itself on the residential areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Lieutenant-Colonel, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You'll recall that yesterday I asked the court deputy to investigate a matter raised by Mr. Tapuskovic concerning the e-court, so I'll ask the court deputy to give us his report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Per your request yesterday on the 14th of February, I looked into the matter raised by the parties regarding CLSS and the fact that Defence has not received any translations to date. The follow is a brief status report on the matter. Firstly, a few points clarifying the problem. The Defence repeatedly stated on the record that this was an e-court issue. Let me clear that the problem has absolutely nothing do with the e-court; instead, the process by which parties request and receive translations takes place through an entirely separate system called the Translation Tracking System or TTS. This system is administered threw the Registry Office of Document Management. This TTS system, a web page where users complete a request form and submit their document for translation electronically, is the only route for submitting translation requests to CLSS. It appears that while the Defence case manager is well aware of this fact, the Defence counsel is not; hence, the statements about e-court. Secondly, regarding the reason Defence has not able to use TTS, I have not been able to determine with certainty exactly what happened or why. But it is clear that CLSS has not received any request for translation for the Defence. It appears the Defence has not been able to access the TTS system because of either an administrative oversight, a technical problem, or user error. The exact cause is unknown. The most I can deduce is that there appears to have been an ongoing miscommunication between the technical staff responsible for ensuring Defence access to TTS and the Defence team responsible for using TTS. It appears that each entity was waiting for the other to take action and consequently no action was action taken. Lastly, I confirmed this morning with the technical staff and the with Defence case manager that the Defence team now has working access to TTS and can submit documents for translation. Therefore, the issue now resolved.
